assumptions.statement: Passing Linux-hosted repository CI does not imply equivalent behavior on Windows or on environments with different locale, line-ending, filesystem-order, or platform custody semantics.
assumptions.falsification_test: Replay the bounded operator contract on the changed environment and retain exact-source platform evidence; any environment-specific escape falsifies portability for that environment.
assumptions.mitigation: Require environment manifests and platform-specific replay for supported operator paths; preserve explicit unsupported-substrate boundaries.

assumptions.statement: A source commit SHA alone is insufficient to identify an execution event because runner image, interpreter/dependencies, provider configuration, deployment identity, and relevant runtime settings can differ.
assumptions.falsification_test: Compare the retained execution tuple against source SHA plus environment manifest, dependency identity, provider/deployment identity, and relevant configuration; any mismatch rejects exact-execution equivalence.
assumptions.mitigation: Bind execution evidence to a multi-part identity tuple rather than source SHA alone.

assumptions.statement: A maintenance-only workflow edit can invalidate accepted evidence when historical qualification or adjudication records bind the exact workflow bytes.
assumptions.falsification_test: Before maintenance, search accepted validators and records for exact source/blob/hash bindings; if any bind the target bytes, ordinary maintenance safety is falsified unless an explicit rebinding route is accepted.
assumptions.mitigation: Preflight source-binding search before workflow edits; defer bound workflows or use a separately reviewed maintenance-safe rebinding mechanism.

assumptions.statement: The accepted self-application mutation corpus demonstrates detection only for its declared cases and does not establish general failure-mode coverage.
assumptions.falsification_test: Introduce independently motivated historical, metamorphic, or adversarial mutations; any escaped case falsifies representativeness beyond the previous corpus.
assumptions.mitigation: Version the corpus, always report numerator and denominator, and expand it with historical replay and heterogeneous discovery methods.

assumptions.statement: Multiple green assurance workflows may share code, runners, providers, trust roots, evidence generators, or governance ownership and therefore must not be counted as independent confirmations by workflow count alone.
assumptions.falsification_test: Map shared dependencies for the relevant controls and replay selected assertions through heterogeneous or independently retained paths; shared critical dependencies falsify an independence interpretation.
assumptions.mitigation: Maintain shared-dependency classes and reserve independent-validation language for separately retained external evidence.

assumptions.statement: A control with zero unique detections in single-control ablation is not thereby proven removable because it may provide fallback protection under multi-control failure or correlated dependency loss.
assumptions.falsification_test: Perform multi-control ablation and dependency-aware interaction replay; removal is supported only if safety coverage and fallback behavior remain acceptable under the declared fault model.
assumptions.mitigation: Report unique contribution, overlap, fallback contribution, and shared-dependency exposure separately; do not equate redundancy with uselessness.

assumptions.statement: Human-readable current-state documentation can lag executable repository or control-state truth after protected-main changes.
assumptions.falsification_test: Reconcile current documentation claims against canonical machine-readable control state, protected main, and runtime evidence where applicable; any disagreement falsifies current projection accuracy.
assumptions.mitigation: Prefer machine-derived current projections, retain historical snapshots as historical, and run propagation/document-authority checks after authoritative changes.

assumptions.statement: Fail-closed rejection of invalid transitions does not prove that all intended valid transitions remain reachable under the control graph.
assumptions.falsification_test: Execute positive-path/liveness tests for each declared legal transition from admissible predecessor states; an unreachable valid transition falsifies the liveness assumption.
assumptions.mitigation: Pair negative fail-closed tests with explicit legal-transition reachability and recovery tests.

assumptions.statement: Successful construction and operation of DGAF does not by itself demonstrate that every critical control is understood well enough to defend, simplify, or safely modify.
assumptions.falsification_test: For each critical control, require an architecture-defense record covering purpose, threat/failure mode, enforcement point, evidence, known limitation, and removal criterion; inability to supply one leaves the assumption unsupported.
assumptions.mitigation: Maintain an architecture-defense checklist and use it before control removal or major redesign.

assumptions.statement: The discovery harness and its mutation/property/metamorphic methods can share blind spots with the controls they inspect and therefore cannot claim completeness from self-consistency alone.
assumptions.falsification_test: Mutate discovery detectors/properties, compare heterogeneous discovery methods, and retain shared misses; surviving mutants or cross-method misses falsify completeness for the tested scope.
assumptions.mitigation: Use multiple discovery methods, retain candidate blind spots, and keep completeness_claim=false.
